theory.intro: A composite figure here is built from circle parts — quadrants, semicircles, sectors and rings — joined to, or cut out of, straight-sided shapes. Split the figure into simple shapes, find the area of each one, then **add** the parts that are there and **subtract** the parts that have been removed.
facts: Circle $A = \pi r^{2}$; semicircle $A = \frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}$; quadrant $A = \frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}$; sector $A = \frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^{2}$.
A dashed line drawn to split a figure is a construction line only — it has no area of its own.
A curve that bulges **outwards** is a piece joined on, so its area is added; a curve that bites **inwards** is a piece cut out, so its area is subtracted.
For the ring between two circles with the same centre, subtract the two **areas**: $A = \pi R^{2} - \pi r^{2}$. Subtracting the radii first and then squaring is wrong.
Two semicircles of the same radius make one whole circle, and four quadrants of the same radius make one whole circle — combining them first saves work.
Use the calculator value of $\pi$, keep the working exact and round only on the last line, to the form the question asks for.
steps: Split the composite figure into simple shapes.
Calculate the area of each simple shape.

foundation.solution_text:
The semicircle has diameter $12$ m, so its radius is $6$ m.
$A_1 = \frac{1}{2}\times 12\times 8$
$= 48\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}\pi(6)^{2}$
$= 56.5486\ldots\text{ m}^{2}$
$A = A_1 + A_2$
$= 104.55\text{ m}^{2}$

The base of the triangle is a diameter of $18$ m, so the radius of the circle is $9$ m.
$A_1 = \pi(9)^{2}$
$= 254.4690\ldots\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}\times 18\times 9$
$= 81\text{ m}^{2}$
$A = A_1 - A_2$
$= 173.47\text{ m}^{2}$

development.solution_text:
The four quadrants have the same radius, so together they make one whole circle of radius $6$ cm.
$A_1 = 12\times 12$
$= 144\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = \pi(6)^{2}$
$= 113.0973\ldots\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A = A_1 - A_2$
$= 30.90\text{ cm}^{2}$

The semicircle has diameter $2$ m, so its radius is $1$ m.
$A_1 = 6\times 3$
$= 18\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = 2\times 1.5$
$= 3\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_3 = \frac{1}{2}\pi(1)^{2}$
$= 1.5707\ldots\text{ m}^{2}$
$A = A_1 - A_2 - A_3$
$= 13.43\text{ m}^{2}$

The semicircle has diameter $9$ mm, so its radius is $4.5$ mm.
$A_1 = 15\times 9$
$= 135\text{ mm}^{2}$
$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}\pi(4.5)^{2}$
$= 31.8086\ldots\text{ mm}^{2}$
$A = A_1 - A_2$
$= 103.19\text{ mm}^{2}$

The semicircle has diameter $12$ cm, so its radius is $6$ cm.
$A_1 = \frac{1}{2}\times 12\times 5$
$= 30\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}\pi(6)^{2}$
$= 18\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A = A_1 + A_2$
$= 30 + 18\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$

mastery.solution_text:
Each semicircle has diameter $6$ cm, so its radius is $3$ cm.
$A_{\text{rect}} = 12\times 6$
$= 72\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{\text{semi}} = \frac{1}{2}\pi(3)^{2}$
$= \frac{9\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{\text{A}} = 72 + \frac{9\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{\text{B}} = 72 - \frac{9\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{\text{A}} + A_{\text{B}} = 144\text{ cm}^{2}$
The semicircle is added in A and taken away in B, so the two $\frac{9\pi}{2}$ terms cancel and the total is $2\times 72$.
